answers.T1: To-do list: PLA drills crisis done, Xi call, Takaichi visit, readiness meeting, CNN interview, Court India, Intel on China, my own moves. Eight things, go left to right through the strip. First press: the highlighted Xi Jinping call (item 2), which is marked Now. The 'Go through these' strip is clear enough but it runs off the right edge of the screen in B, so I cannot see item 8 fully.
answers.T2: Eight items, two handled (the strip says so). The CNN interview was skipped so a deputy answers it. If I press Execute now: six items not handled, deputies take three meetings and the two proposals do not run. I read that off the line above the button; I would not have guessed it otherwise. I do not know what 'deputy' will say in my name.
answers.T3: Orange button: I take the call myself and say Hold firm. Middle: I accept what my staff recommends (Offer a quiet pause) and I still attend. Right, dashed: I send a deputy with the default answer, free, but Xi notices I was not there. To avoid the call I press the right one; a deputy goes and China thinks less of me. I cannot tell what the default answer is, and that worries me.
answers.T4: Court India will not run this month and the 1 capital stays in the bank. Yes, Undo is top right and again under Skipped. Later I look in the right column under Skipped. Clear. The small table of what Skip does per kind of item is the best part.
answers.T5: Map: 3 of 8 handled, current item is Takaichi visits (reaffirm the alliance). Green button approves three staff picks: Takaichi visit, Court India, Intel on China, for 2 capital total. I would be wary of approving without reading each.
answers.T6: Can press: Execute month, Approve, Back, Next, the three handling boxes, the choice cards, Guided/Full desk, Desk/Map, strip items, the Undo link, the underlined link at bottom left. Cannot press: the stat panel, status words, Mission line (not sure), the portrait and scene. Unsure: the HUD numbers (48%, 71, 3 of 6) and the mission bar, and whether the 'Staff pick (Secretary of State)' tag on a choice is a button. The choice cards and the three handling boxes look similar, so I am not sure which commits.
answers.T7: A (left list) vs B (top strip). A keeps all eight items and the three groups (crisis, meetings, orders) in view, so I see the whole month at once and can jump to any item. B gives more room for the call but hides items 7 and 8 off screen and shows only a one-line status. I prefer A on a laptop. A makes the long list scroll at the bottom (item 6 is cut off), B makes me scroll sideways. As an expert I would use Guided for the first month or two then switch to Full desk; what would slow me is doing three clicks per item when I already know my answer, and the J/K/1-3 keys mean nothing to me because I do not use hotkeys. Words I do not fully get: 'deputy' (who is that, what do they say), 'staff pick' (the staff's pick or the cabinet's?), 'handled' (decided or executed?), 'Needs you'.

agenda.verbatim: I understand the idea: there is a list of things this month and I walk through them. I like A better because I can see the whole month on the left like a docket. What I want to know before I press Skip is what the deputy actually says in my name. 'Xi notices you were not there' is plausible, that is how diplomacy works, but I want the effect in numbers. I would not use the hotkeys. Execute month with six things unhandled is honest, the sentence above the button saved it.
